answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the ember hash is checked against the haven checkpoint at intake, the beacon audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Scaling to 635 identities multiplies that fee by 864 with no matching gain in influence. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
